title: Total-limit comparison and transposes of augmented tower arrows
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $u^*\dashv P=Ru_*$ for the canonical derived adjunction, with counit $\varepsilon$ and ordinary derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, use strict constant-$A$ towers on the small diagram sites [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], and let $\Delta$ be the constant-tower functor, $G=u^*$ termwise, $P^J=Ru_*^J$, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Normalize $\mathcal L_T\Delta\cong1$ on diagonal K-injective representatives and derive the adjunction $\Delta\dashv\lim$ from the ordinary module adjunction. Let
$$a_V:P\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}P^JV$$
be exactly the derived comparison from $u_*\lim=\lim u_*^J$ in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. For every $V\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_{\mathcal X})))$ and $M\in D_{\mathcal Y}$ the composite bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}P^JV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta M,P^JV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G\Delta M,V)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta u^*M,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u^*M,\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V)$$
is the ordinary adjunction bijection after postcomposition with $a_V^{-1}$. Explicitly, for any tower objects $Z$ over $\mathcal Y$, $V$ over $\mathcal X$, arrow $b:GZ\to V$ with tower adjunct $b^\sharp:Z\to P^JV$, and $j:\Delta M\to Z$, the ordinary adjunct of the limit of $b\circ G(j)$ is
$$a_V^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(b^\sharp)\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(j):M\longrightarrow P\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V.$$
Here the source of the limit map is identified with $u^*M$ by $G\Delta=\Delta u^*$ and $\mathcal L\Delta=1$. This equality includes the actual counits and is natural in all displayed arguments. No perfectness, completeness or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Use the supplied exact module adjunction d.moduleAdj and its termwise tower adjunction. Constant towers, evaluation, and termwise inverse image are exact by levelwise abelianity [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Their canonical derived functors and the descended constant interchange are given by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The module and tower categories have K-injective resolutions using the existing Grothendieck instances [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck, lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck, lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective].

For any exact left adjoint F with right adjoint U, [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] give the two cochain-level unit and counit equations for the specified canonical derived adjunction. Expand the canonical cochainUnit only through the quotient factorization isomorphisms. Naturality of the first counit gives the corresponding equation for a composite of two adjunctions; this equation holds on every complex, without a K-injective hypothesis.

Let a be the conjugate isomorphism of constantInterchange under the composite adjunctions (moduleAdjunction followed by the source constant-limit adjunction) and (target constant-limit adjunction followed by towerAdjunction). To check the representative equation, transpose under the latter adjunction. Use its counit equation, naturality of constantInterchange, and the composite counit equations from step 2. The localization factorization of constantInterchange is exactly its three defining factors and the exact-localization composition equations. At the cochain level the conjugate is the ordinary preservation-of-limits comparison: compose with each ordinary limit projection, use naturality of the ordinary module counit, and apply the module adjunction triangle identity. Thus the conjugate equals preservesLimitNatIso. This proves precisely the first displayed equation for a, on every complex, and fixes the prescribed common-underived-composite normalization.

Evaluation at op 0 is exact and left adjoint to the constant functor, with tower unit induced by the unique maps n to 0. Hence constants preserve K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. On a K-injective complex H, the cochainUnit for limit applied to the constant complex is an isomorphism. The ordinary constant-limit unit is an isomorphism because the constant functor on the nonempty connected tower index is fully faithful. The localized unit equation of step 2 therefore makes the derived constant-limit unit invertible at QH. Transport along a K-injective resolution of every derived object and use naturality to conclude its invertibility everywhere. The same unit equation is exactly both ConstantUnitNormalization clauses.

For adjunctions a and b and an isomorphism e between their left adjoints, naturality and unit_conjugateEquiv give b.homEquiv(e;f)=a.homEquiv(f);conjugate(e). Apply this to the two composite derived adjunctions and constantInterchange, and cancel its invertible component on the right. This is the universal Hom equality in the theorem. Substitute f=constantInterchange inverse followed by G(j) and b. Naturality in the source of the tower adjunction replaces the transpose of G(j);b by j followed by the transpose of b. Expand the constant-limit homEquiv as its unit followed by the image of the map, and cancel a once more. This is exactly the final augmented-arrow formula, with the actual derived unit visible.
